# Hermes media integration handover

Prepared 2026-09-14 for a follow-up session. This is a handover, not authorization
for additional live changes.

## Goal and remaining work

Hermes on ai-dev should read household playback history and eventually manage
Sonarr, Radarr, and Lidarr through human-approved conversations in **Moshi iOS
and Photon iMessage**. Do not substitute Seerr or an external approval page.

The read-only Plex/Tautulli and Arr phase is deployed and verified. Remaining:

1. Add Jellyfin playback history, including reporting setup if still absent.
2. Design and implement independently verified conversational approvals.
3. Introduce a small set of approved Arr mutations. Deletion comes last.

Recommended order: Jellyfin history, approval-channel feasibility, then narrow
Arr mutations. Direct Portainer Git-source linkage is optional future work,
not a prerequisite for either feature.

## Start the next session here

1. Fetch current main and inspect the working tree before changing anything.
   Do not blindly resume an old feature branch or overwrite this handover.
2. Read this file, `docs/hermes-media.md`, `docs/ai-dev.md`,
   `docs/docker-deployment.md`, and `services/media-broker/README.md`.
3. Confirm the desired next phase with the owner and obtain authorization for
   its live changes, including plugin installation or service restarts.
4. Recheck live versions, channel capabilities, and plugin state. The observations
   below are dated evidence, not a promise that infrastructure is unchanged.
5. Use one Luna implementation writer and a fresh independent reviewer. Discover
   currently available agents/models before dispatch. The parent owns acceptance,
   publication, merges, and live operations. Do not silently switch execution
   protocols when a governed subagent lane fails.

At handover preparation, GitHub confirmed PR #1755 was merged. A subsequent
`git fetch origin main` timed out, so the checkout was not updated to that merge.
The local branch remained `docs/media-broker-image-only-updates` at
`05f2af4b23ea65fabfc2a32e3ee59dcd56ac0237`. This handover was then added locally;
it has not been committed or pushed by this session.

## Completed work and release references

- [PR #1753](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra/pull/1753): read-only broker,
  sanitized Docker observer, host policy, and Hermes integration.
  Merged as `5dc476a3e1338250ba722113811c8cebf645efaa`.
- [PR #1754](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra/pull/1754): Portainer ownership,
  CI coverage, and dependency security patches.
  Merged as `1cd26015002c8f24e8148f227d10e5eb2005136a`.
- [PR #1755](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra/pull/1755): image-only Portainer
  update procedure discovered during the live rollout. **Now merged**, as
  `e8f53c5ec4b381b350cd7b67fa309d2ba45ea1a6`.
- [Production verification comment](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra/pull/1754#issuecomment-5659179639)
  records the patched deployment and Portainer rebuild trap.

There is no outstanding documentation-merge housekeeping item from this phase.

### Last verified production state

- Portainer manages stack `media-broker`, assigned ID **39**, endpoint **3**.
  Container name remains `media-broker-candidate`; the name does not mean it is
  undeployed. Look up IDs again after a restore.
- Stack active, container healthy, MCP **1.28.1** verified inside the container.
- Running image matched the image explicitly built on docker-host from merged
  source `1cd2601`:
  `sha256:2d5193e7d34d5433e02b81d6a6c6d308b768ca6f811f75d85ee8f690498bb13b`.
- Exactly four read-only tools: `arr_library_inventory`, `arr_quality_profiles`,
  `arr_root_folders`, and `tautulli_play_history`.
- Hermes successfully read inventory, profiles, and root folders for all three
  Arr services. A historical Tautulli track query returned one record; only the
  count was reported, not the playback record.
- Unauthenticated requests returned 401; an untrusted Origin returned 403.
  The non-ai-dev laptop could not connect to broker TCP 8765.
- Nonroot/read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, exact
  private bind, and five read-only secret mounts passed runtime checks. No raw
  credential values appeared in the container environment.
- Hermes user gateway remained active with zero restarts. No new gateway restart
  or credential rotation was needed for the patch deployment.
- Expected and running application project sets matched, 15 projects each,
  during ownership handoff. This checks project presence, not ownership of every
  unrelated application in Portainer.
- GitHub reported zero open Dependabot alerts after the security merge. Recheck
  current advisories before the next release.

## Deployment rules that must not be lost

**The broker is Portainer-managed, manually updated, and NOT Git-connected.**
Git remains the canonical source of the application and Compose definition.

Two Portainer 2.45 behaviors were discovered live:

1. Polling belongs to the shared Git source. Creating the broker with
   `AutoUpdate: null` reused source ID 1 and inherited its five-minute polling.
   That scheduler tried an unwanted image pull. Detaching only the broker
   removed its Git workflow, AutoUpdate, and webhook. The other stacks' shared
   five-minute source was left unchanged. Do not reconnect the broker to it or
   disable unrelated stacks' polling as a workaround.
2. A manual update with the canonical `build` block still present rebuilt from
   Portainer's retained old Git context, even with `PullImage: false`. This
   replaced the prepared image with old source. The image-ID acceptance check
   caught it; a healthy container alone would not have.

The working procedure, detailed in `docs/hermes-media.md`, is:

- Check out reviewed source in the root-owned host directory.
- Run host preflight, then explicitly build locked source against
  `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`. Record the built image ID.
- Create an **image-only Portainer deployment copy** by removing only
  `services.media-broker.build` and its `context`/`dockerfile` children.
  Keep the canonical build block in Git and the host checkout.
- Preserve every other runtime/security field and existing nonsecret settings.
  Update only the intended stack through authenticated Portainer operations.
  Set `PullImage: false`, `Prune: false`, with no automatic updates or webhook.
- Require controller completion, health, the exact recorded running image ID,
  the intended installed dependency version, and authenticated application reads.

Do not use the standalone candidate launcher after Portainer takes ownership.
That would create a second deployment controller. Do not assume Portainer runs
preflight, rebuilds the right checkout, or respects per-stack polling isolation.

## Security boundaries and sensitive data

- Backend API keys and the broker bearer remain in host-owned files outside
  Hermes. No raw upstream passthrough or write tools are currently exposed.
- Never print credentials, messages, or individual household playback records.
  Report counts/status only during live verification.
- Preserve Photon/Moshi configuration, unrelated firewall policy, existing
  tokens, and the functioning Docker observer.
- Broker endpoint: `http://docker-host:8765/mcp`. Exact Host
  `docker-host:8765`; exact Origin `http://docker-host:8765`.
- docker-host binds only its verified Tailscale IPv4. The source-pinned
  `DOCKER-USER` exception admits ai-dev through `tailscale0` before the
  unconditional broker-port drop and general established-connection rules.
  ai-dev has corresponding exact endpoint egress. Keep both host firewall and
  Tailscale grant checks. No Traefik/shared 443 or LAN exception was added.
- The broker runs as `65532:65532` with five read-only secret mounts, no Docker
  socket, and no media mounts. The 5 MiB response bound accommodates the observed
  approximately 2.27 MiB Lidarr inventory.
- The Docker observer on port 2375 has no socket. It exposes only bounded,
  sanitized reads through a private socket backend. Its separate non-internal
  frontend is necessary for Docker host-port publication. The backend remains
  internal-only. Preserve this topology and source checksum validation.

## Live locations and access notes

Repository: `/Users/mm/dev/home-infra`.

| --- | --- |
| docker-host | `100.96.174.126`; authorized SSH account used was `mm@docker-host`, with passwordless sudo |
| ai-dev | `100.84.159.38`; SSH alias `ai-dev`, management user `michael` |

| Hermes integration helper | `/home/hermes/.local/bin/manage-hermes-media.py` |

Secret files are `broker-token`, `sonarr-api-key`, `radarr-api-key`,
`lidarr-api-key`, and `tautulli-api-key`. Directories are root:65532 mode 0750;
files are root:65532 mode 0640. File-backed Compose secret declarations do not
set host permissions. Do not rotate or copy these into chat.

The ignored local `.envrc` contains `PORTAINER_API` and was mode 0600. If needed,
parse its literal assignment without shell evaluation. Pass the API credential
through protected stdin to remote Python, never command arguments or output.
The local Portainer API is `https://127.0.0.1:9443` on docker-host. Prior operations
used it through SSH. Never dump full stack/container metadata containing env.

Hermes runs a **user** gateway unit, not a root system unit. Its UID was 30033:

```sh
sudo -n -u hermes env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/30033 \
  systemctl --user status hermes-gateway.service
```

Use explicit Bash/Python for ai-dev remote commands; its login shell is fish.
Check status without printing message-bearing journals into the conversation.

Protected rollback/evidence locations on docker-host:

- `/var/lib/hermes-rollout/security-1cd2601`: prior source, old/new image IDs,
  build log, saved controller definition, image-only deployment copy, and
  `runtime-verified.json`.
- `/var/lib/hermes-rollout/observer-31da1267c641`: earlier observer/firewall
  backups and Portainer adoption/detach metadata.
- Old image tag `home-infra/media-broker:rollback-5dc476a` was retained for

## Jellyfin history work

The earlier audit found the Playback Reporting plugin absent. Recheck before
installing anything; the current broker has no Jellyfin adapter.

Plan:

1. Establish installed Jellyfin version, supported reporting-plugin version,
   current activity/playback data, storage, and backup/retention requirements.
2. Obtain approval for plugin installation and any Jellyfin restart. Determine
   exactly what can be queried and whether useful old records already exist.
   Do not promise backfill. Reliable collection may start only at enablement.
3. Select the narrowest usable authentication and keep its credential in a new
   host-managed broker secret, not Hermes or Portainer environment values.
4. Implement a read-only adapter with exact endpoint allow-listing, bounded
   requests/results/date ranges, no redirects or environment proxies, sanitized
   errors, and explicit source identification.
5. Test movies, episodes, music, user attribution, time zones, pagination,
   sessions versus completed plays, missing records, authorization failures, and
   empty results. Distinguish Jellyfin records from Plex/Tautulli records.
6. Review, merge with authorization, preflight/build, and deploy using the
   image-only Portainer procedure. Verify live using counts only.

An empty query does not prove that no playback occurred. Avoid claiming complete
household history until collection and retention coverage are established.

## Conversation-approved Arr mutations

This requires a new authorization boundary, not just enabling native prompts.
Earlier research found Hermes/Moshi/Photon native confirmation mechanisms are
not independently enforced against a compromised or instruction-following
Hermes process with the same UID and access to its files.

Required design:

- Hermes proposes an immutable, exact plan. The plan identifies service, target
  IDs, intended values, relevant previous state, and expected side effects.
- A separately owned service keeps authoritative plan state and validates
  human approval. Hermes must not be able to create approval evidence, edit the
  verifier's state, access its credentials, or invoke an ungated write path.
- Approval arrives inside Moshi or Photon from a verified authorized human,
  bound to the correct conversation and plan. A text string such as "yes",
  supplied or quoted by the agent, is not evidence of approval.
- Bind approvals to plan identity/content, expiration, and one-time consumption.
  Recheck target state immediately before execution. Changed plans or relevant
  state require fresh approval. Handle retries without duplicate side effects.
- Give the executor only explicitly supported typed actions. Keep backend keys
  outside Hermes and avoid generic URL, method, or arbitrary-payload forwarding.
- Maintain a restricted audit trail without leaking credentials or household
  message/playback contents into ordinary logs.

First investigate the actual trusted ingress available in each channel. Verify
sender identity, message provenance, replay protection, and separation from
agent-controlled credentials. Do not assume either channel supplies signed
callbacks or an adequate independent approval API. If neither can provide a
trustworthy path, present that blocker and design choices to the owner rather
than pretending the normal confirmation dialog solves it.

Suggested initial scope, to agree with the owner:

- Add an explicitly identified movie, series, or artist.
- Change monitoring state or an explicitly named quality profile for one target.
- Treat immediate searching/downloading, root-folder changes, moves, rescans,
  and bulk operations as separate side effects requiring explicit scope.
- Exclude deletion and destructive filesystem operations initially.

Tests must cover forged/quoted approvals, agent-originated echoes, wrong sender
or conversation, expired/replayed approvals, plan tampering, stale library
state, concurrency, partial failure, retry/idempotency, and direct bypass of the
verifier. Start with dry-run plans and a tightly bounded live action only after
independent review and owner authorization.

## Code and validation pointers

- Broker: `services/media-broker/src/media_broker/{server,config,adapters}.py`
- Broker tests: `services/media-broker/tests/test_broker.py`

  `tests/agent-observer_test.py`

Use **uv 0.12.5**, not an arbitrary installed uv version, for locked validation.
The accepted lock resolved MCP 1.28.1, pytest 9.0.3, and pytest-asyncio 1.3.0.
The latter was necessary because 1.2.0 excludes pytest 9. All 25 broker tests,
Ruff, packaging/preflight, isolated Docker smoke, and CI passed. Three upstream
warning messages remained. Advisory-specific exploit tests were not added;
transport/task non-use was also inspected independently.

Earlier research and review artifacts are local, not repository files. Relevant
reports live under:

`/Users/mm/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-mm-dev-home-infra--/subagent-artifacts/outputs/`

- `4056cd7f-0efa-4ebf-9814-7599a2ee2bd2/media-wiring-plan.md`
- `726853de-f4e7-46d8-abc9-f1585991afe0/approval-isolation.md`

- `0772e700-ddd7-455b-9ac5-3b4e9cc10a3b/promotion-review.md`

Treat older plans as historical evidence. The Portainer live findings and
merged runbook override any earlier recommendation for ordinary shared Git
polling or uploading the unchanged build-bearing Compose definition.

## Addendum 2026-09-14: Jellyfin history phase deferred by owner decision

The owner selected the deferral option after this session's read-only audit.
No live Jellyfin changes were made: no plugin installation, no restart, no
credential creation, and no broker changes. Repository state at audit time was
clean `main` at `e8f53c5` matching `origin/main` (the PR #1755 merge), with only
this untracked handover file present.

### Verified live state (aggregate facts only)

- Jellyfin `10.11.11`, image digest `sha256:aefb67e6...b35db`, matching the
  compose pin; container healthy.
- Playback Reporting plugin absent, rechecked before any recommendation.
- No structured playback history exists in `jellyfin.db`: only unstructured
  ActivityLog text events (about 3,590 playback start/stop rows since
  2025-05-02) and per-item UserData play states. Any future collection starts
  at enablement; no backfill is possible.
- Broker and Jellyfin share the `proxy` Docker network, so a future adapter
  needs no new reachability work (`http://jellyfin:8096`).

### Why deferred: upstream plugin is broken on this exact server version

- Jellyfin 10.11.9+ removed `IUserManager.Users`, breaking many plugins at
  runtime with `MissingMethodException`.
- Playback Reporting fixed this in v18 (tag commit `e899995`), but v18 was
  never fully released to the stable channel (plugin issue #133, open).
- The stable catalog (verified via the repo.jellyfin.org manifest on
  2026-09-14) offers only v17.0.0.0 (`targetAbi 10.11.0.0`, reported broken on
  10.11.9+ by open issues #128 and #135) and v19.0.0.0 (`targetAbi 12.0.0.0`,
  Jellyfin 12 preview only). Plugin GUID
  `5c534381-91a3-43cb-907a-35aa02eb9d2c`.
- The community workaround is an untrusted third-party DLL zip; rejected.
- Considered and rejected: downgrading Jellyfin to 10.11.8, building history
  from text-only ActivityLog polling, and adding a webhook push path.

### Resume conditions and first steps

Resume when either a stable-channel Playback Reporting release targets the
running 10.11.x line, or the server moves to a Jellyfin 12 release with plugin
v19 available. Re-verify rather than trusting this addendum:

1. Recheck the plugin's catalog entry and the state of issues #128, #133, and
   #135, plus the installed Jellyfin version and digest pin.
2. Re-obtain owner authorization for plugin installation and any restart.
3. Then follow the original plan: dedicated Jellyfin API key in a new
   host-managed broker secret (`/etc/media-broker/secrets`), read-only adapter
   with exact endpoint allow-listing and bounded requests/results, counts-only
   live verification, image-only Portainer deployment.

Session hygiene note: one early ActivityLog query printed event text into the
conversation before the counts-only discipline was applied. No credentials or
tokens were involved. Future live queries against household data must project
aggregate counts only.

# media-broker

Read-only MCP broker for household media services. This repository owns the
application source, its tests, and the published container image. The
production deployment (Portainer stack, host firewall, secret files) is owned
by the [`mich-murphy/home-infra`](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra)
repository; see its `docs/hermes-media.md` for the deployment runbook.

This project exposes a small MCP server over the official Python SDK's
Streamable HTTP transport. The adapters target Sonarr 4.0.19 (API v3), Radarr
6.3.0 (API v3), Lidarr 3.1.0 (API v1), and Tautulli 2.18.1. It has four tools:

- `arr_library_inventory` (Sonarr, Radarr, or Lidarr; bounded local pagination)
- `arr_quality_profiles`
- `arr_root_folders`
- `tautulli_play_history` (movie, episode, or track; inclusive maximum 31-day range and optional numeric user filter)

There are no write tools, generic upstream requests, approval endpoints, Seerr,
or Jellyfin integrations. Arr APIs return arrays, so inventory pagination is
performed after one bounded response and reports that fact honestly.

Short answer: that file doesn't test the image or the app — those tests moved. It tests the three things that still live *in this repo* and can only break here: the compose contract, the firewall policy, and the inventory. But your skepticism is partly correct — there is some duplication. Here's the honest breakdown of every block in it:

## What it uniquely covers (would be lost if deleted)

1. **No `build:` block on the service** — this is the regression guard for the Portainer 2.45 stale-Git-context rebuild incident documented in `docs/hermes-media.md`. Now that the image is pulled from GHCR, a re-added build block is precisely the failure mode that silently swaps in a stale build. Nothing else checks this.
2. **Image ref pinned to `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main(@sha256:…)`** — the deploy trigger is Renovate's digest bump; change the tag or registry and auto-deploy silently stops. This is the only pin on that model.
3. **Fail-closed bind variables** (`MEDIA_BROKER_BIND`, `_BIND_HOST`, `_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND` all `:?` with no default) — `docker-hardening.sh` renders with permissive CI placeholders, so it structurally cannot catch a default value sneaking in and opening a public bind.
4. **`ansible/roles/docker-host/tasks/published-ports.yaml`** — drop-before-established ordering in DOCKER-USER, the `[443, 2375, 8006]` port exclusion, rule present only when enabled. This is live firewall config and has **zero other test coverage**. The firewall doesn't care where the image is built.
5. **Negative fixture for `check-portainer-drift.sh`** (missing compose path must fail) — the only test of the drift script itself.

## Where you're right (duplication I can remove)

- The `no-new-privileges` and `cap_drop ALL` assertions duplicate `docker-hardening.sh`, which renders and checks every service in every stack — including this compose file.
- The direct `check-portainer-drift.sh --source-only` call duplicates a standalone step already in the quality gate (the negative fixture is the only part that's unique).
- The pinned config *values* (`docker-host:8765` Host/Origin, the 5 MiB bound) are this repo's settings, but pinning exact strings is arguably double-entry bookkeeping rather than behavior testing.

- **B. Trim the duplication** — drop the NNP/cap_drop/direct-drift assertions, keep 1–5 above.

**The broker is Portainer-managed, manually updated, and NOT Git-connected.**
Git remains the canonical source of the application and Compose definition.

   caught it; a healthy container alone would not have.

- Check out reviewed source in the root-owned host directory.

## Conversation-approved Arr mutations

This requires a new authorization boundary, not just enabling native prompts.
Earlier research found Hermes/Moshi/Photon native confirmation mechanisms are
not independently enforced against a compromised or instruction-following
Hermes process with the same UID and access to its files.

Required design:

- Hermes proposes an immutable, exact plan identifying service, target IDs,
  intended values, relevant previous state, and expected side effects.
- A separately owned service keeps authoritative plan state and validates
  human approval. Hermes must not be able to create approval evidence, edit
  the verifier's state, access its credentials, or invoke an ungated write
  path.
- Approval arrives inside Moshi or Photon from a verified authorized human,
  bound to the correct conversation and plan. A text string such as "yes",
  supplied or quoted by the agent, is not evidence of approval.
- Bind approvals to plan identity/content, expiration, and one-time
  consumption. Recheck target state immediately before execution. Changed
  plans or relevant state require fresh approval. Handle retries without
  duplicate side effects.
- Give the executor only explicitly supported typed actions. Keep backend
  keys outside Hermes; avoid generic URL, method, or arbitrary-payload
  forwarding.
- Maintain a restricted audit trail without leaking credentials or household
  message/playback contents into ordinary logs.

First investigate the actual trusted ingress available in each channel:
sender identity, message provenance, replay protection, separation from
agent-controlled credentials. Do not assume either channel supplies signed
callbacks or an adequate independent approval API. If neither can provide a
trustworthy path, present that blocker and design choices to the owner rather
than pretending the normal confirmation dialog solves it.

operations as separate side effects requiring explicit scope. Exclude

library state, concurrency, partial failure, retry/idempotency, and direct
bypass of the verifier. Start with dry-run plans and a tightly bounded live
action only after independent review and owner authorization.
